candidate_value.supporting_text: Students were randomized individually at initial platform registration across three independent dimensions: topic, AI versus CAL-only support, and mastery versus non-mastery progression. Each assignment had equal probability, teachers and students did not know assignments in advance, and reported baseline characteristics in the delayed-test sample were generally balanced. Exact software sequence-generation details were not reported, but no material randomization failure signal was identified.

candidate_value.domain_label: Participant flow, exposure and post-randomization selection
candidate_value.supporting_text: The week-1 analysis sample contained 6,997 students and 6,327 completed the delayed assessment. Exercise 1 was reached by nearly all platform entrants, but treatment changed pace and progression to later content. The authors explicitly document these exposure and selection complications. Delayed non-participation and the post-mistake event sample require separate result-level appraisal.

candidate_value.supporting_text: Platform progression, practice and post-mistake outcomes were defined from logged events. The one-week delayed assessment used four objectively scored items, with practiced versus unpracticed status determined by randomized topic assignment and missing item responses among test takers coded as incorrect. The full appendix documents outcome construction, tables and tutor prompts.

candidate_value.domain_label: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
candidate_value.supporting_text: Although AI assignment was randomized, the reported comparison is restricted to mastery students who generated an observed mistake event. AI altered exposure, pace and the probability and timing of mistakes, so conditioning on mistakes does not preserve the randomized comparison. The unadjusted event-conditioned model is therefore not an appropriate estimator of a full-population effect of assignment.

candidate_value.domain_label: Bias due to missing outcome data
candidate_value.supporting_text: Next-attempt correctness excludes mistake events with no subsequent non-skip submitted attempt. Table 8 reports 13,512 observations for next-attempt correctness versus 14,558 mistake events for the subsequently reached-streak outcome. Because assignment affected pace and continuation, the missing next-attempt outcomes could be related to intervention and prognosis; no dedicated missing-outcome sensitivity analysis was identified.

candidate_value.supporting_text: The paper reports several post-mistake outcomes and robustness decompositions and explicitly limits their causal interpretation. However, the AEA registration record and any separate analysis plan have not yet been independently verified, so prespecification of the exact event-conditioned outcome, exclusions and model cannot be established.

candidate_value.estimand_or_result_scope: Difference between assignment to AI and CAL-only support in correctness of the next non-skip attempt among observed Exercise 1 mistake events in mastery-assigned students, conditional on a subsequent non-skip attempt.
candidate_value.notes: RoB 2 candidate for the normalized post-mistake outcome. Overall high risk applies to causal interpretation because the analysis conditions on a post-randomization event—making a mistake—that AI assignment itself affects, and next-attempt correctness is undefined for events without a subsequent attempt. The authors appropriately describe these estimates as mechanism evidence rather than the primary randomized evidence on learning. The observed platform association remains informative for mechanism generation but should not be treated as an unbiased intent-to-treat learning effect.

candidate_value.domain_label: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
candidate_value.supporting_text: The interventions were delivered through a purpose-built platform and the main factorial regressions estimate effects of assignment. Students and teachers could not be blinded after exposure, but the experienced AI support and progression rule were the intended interventions, and no off-protocol deviations likely to bias the effect-of-assignment estimand were identified.

candidate_value.domain_label: Bias due to missing outcome data
candidate_value.supporting_text: Of 6,997 week-1 platform entrants, 6,327 completed the delayed assessment. Delayed analyses were restricted to test takers; missing item responses were coded incorrect only among those who took the test, while non-takers had no imputed outcome. Completion was high and delayed-sample balance was reassuring, but no all-randomized-participant missing-data sensitivity analysis was identified.

candidate_value.domain_label: Bias in measurement of the outcome
candidate_value.supporting_text: All groups received the same objectively scored four-item delayed assessment. Randomized topic assignment determined which items were practiced or unpracticed, limiting differential classification. The brief test may be statistically imprecise, but that is not in itself differential measurement bias.

candidate_value.domain_label: Bias in selection of the reported result
candidate_value.supporting_text: The paper reports practiced and unpracticed Exercise 1 and Exercise 2 items, totals, differences and several null or robustness results, and it identifies a preregistered AI-by-mastery complementarity hypothesis. The public registration record and any separate analysis plan have not yet been verified against the report, and multiple eligible delayed outcomes and specifications remain; selective-analysis risk cannot be ruled out.

candidate_value.estimand_or_result_scope: Effects of randomized AI support, mastery progression and their interaction on the one-week delayed practiced and unpracticed mathematics assessment outcomes; reported delayed analyses are among week-1 platform entrants who completed the delayed assessment.
candidate_value.notes: RoB 2 appraisal candidate for the normalized one-week delayed assessment bundle. The randomized factorial design and objective assessment support the comparison, but 670 of 6,997 week-1 platform entrants did not complete the delayed assessment and the published delayed analyses exclude those non-takers. Baseline balance in the delayed-test sample is reassuring, while absence of a verified registration/SAP comparison and multiple eligible delayed outcomes leave some selective-analysis uncertainty.
